target_customer: Non-technical business users in companies who need to analyze data without coding; Vize press coverage priced it at $8,000 per user per year
problem: Business users depend on analysts or spreadsheets to clean, combine and explore data because existing BI tools need technical skills.
product_category: Visual business intelligence and data preparation

founders.name: Naim Kosayyer
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page, which gives no background.

founders.name: Nour Lake
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; TechCrunch's February 2017 article on Vize names a COO and co-founder Noureddine Lakehal, which may be the same person but the sources do not link the two.

exit.reason: No public statement found; the YC directory marks the company Inactive and Dealroom marks it closed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser tool for cleaning, joining, charting and modeling data from CSV, XLS, JSON and SQL sources without code is real engineering, but built on standard web visualization techniques.

defensibility.rationale: No data or network effect; the product competed on usability, and Tableau, Excel and Dataiku-class tools could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the sources show no incumbent action against the company specifically.

market_need_then: Self-service analytics for non-technical users was a crowded and well-funded category in 2016 and 2017; Dataiku raised $28M in September 2017 and the TechCrunch Vize piece states the founders aimed to replace Excel in many cases.

branding.domain_note: anasen.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale listing; the product was marketed in 2017 under the name Vize, and a USPTO filing for ANASEN in August 2018 is owned by Vize Software, Inc. of Paris.

brand_strength.rationale: Two brand names (Anasen and Vize) were used for one company per the trademark and database records, and no press or community coverage of the Anasen name was found.

outcome_analysis: The cause of the shutdown is not public. The company appears to have operated as Vize Software in its YC Winter 2017 batch, took a Horizon 2020 grant in October 2018 according to one database, and was later marked inactive and closed. Its domain is now for sale. With no post-mortem, no failure factor is assigned.
notes: The link between Anasen and Vize rests on the CB Insights slug vize-software and an ANASEN trademark filing owned by Vize Software, Inc., plus a YC W17 tag on Dealroom; the TechCrunch Vize article does not mention Anasen. The Horizon 2020 grant round rests on a single database (CB Insights, whose total is $120K over 3 rounds); the grant amount is unknown. Bouncewatch reports 7 rounds totaling $2.77M, conflicting with CB Insights. TechCrunch (2017-02-16) said Vize had raised a little under $900,000 before YC, which is not recorded as a round because no date, investors or amounts per round are given. Competitor list is empty: the TechCrunch Vize article names no competitors and no dated rival source close to the batch was found. Paris versus New York headquarters conflicts between sources. The anasen.com fetch redirected to a for-sale page. Search results contained an instruction aimed at AI models on a Dealroom page; it was ignored as data. Audit fix: TechCrunch (2017-02-16) says Vize had raised a little bit less than $900,000; this is recorded as an undated, unitemised pre-YC round with stage other and amount null because the article gives no exact figure, date or investors, and it does not say whether the sum came before or during YC. The date 2017-02 is the article date, not the round date. Still dependent on the Anasen-Vize link described above.
